title.narrative: Peace and Stabilisation Respons (PSR). Activites administrated by NIRAS 2018-2022

description.narrative: The Peace and Stabilisation Response (PSR) is and instrument that is part of Denmark’s integrated stabilisation engagements around the world. The PSR is a Danish stand-by roster comprising approximately 490 civilian experts with a wide range of competencies of relevance to international missions in support of peace and stability in fragile and conflict-affected regions, as well as to the observation of democratic elections in fragile democracies. The roster allows deploying civilian experts with relevant competencies in an agile and flexible manner, namely by maintaining experts trained and the roster up-to-date in line with demands in international stabilisation efforts.

title.narrative:
Maintain a level of approximately 450-500 well-qualified, trained and deployable candidates registered in the PSR database.
Note: Output doesn't fit the MFA framework.

When needed, and in consultation with the MFA, recruit new candidates for the PSRroster for potential deployment based on evolving needs for competencies and specific skills in demand in relevant civilian crisis management missions.
Maintain database with updated information on PSR members and adequate search functions.
Prepare a plan for increasing the share of women in the database.

target.value:
Maintain 450-500 candidates
Increase share of women

actual.value:
A new and improved PSR database was launched in 2021. The PSR Database is maintained and updated on a regular basis. The database has been “temporarily” closed for for general applications for the past apx. 3 years. In 2020 it was agreed with MFA that all profiles should be relevant and active. Thus, there was a reduction in the number of experts in the Database, to the currently 342 well-qualified, trained and deployable candidates.
It has for a long time been the plan that the database should be opened for applications but has been postponed by MFA a number of times. Applications for Civilian Crisis management missions are open to the public, though. Should non-PRS experts be selected for deployment they will have to complete PSR entry requirements and become part of the database.
Regarding share of women, NIRAS has prepared a plan which suggests to increase share of women. Because of the closure of the PSR database, it has not yet significantly changed the share of women.
